_comment: A cross-conversation ground-truth case study, built from scan_ruling_mentions.py's census + direct transcript reads. This is the answer key for a candidate synthesis benchmark item: 'reconstruct the full story of DECISIONS 0017 from these conversations.' Every event below is a literal quote with conversation id + timestamp, not a summary invented after the fact -- if a candidate model's answer covers these beats with correct chronology and no invented ones, that's the pass bar.

cross_check_against_decisions_md.decisions_md_source_attribution: docs/COWORK_REPORT_projects_reconciliation.md, section 'Drafted DECISIONS 0017' -- confirmed verbatim in seq 4's quote, so the ratified text and the report section are the same artifact, not two independent drafts.

why_this_is_a_good_benchmark_item: It requires reading at least 4-6 separate conversations spanning 11 days to get right -- no single conversation contains the full story.
It has a verifiable ground truth: DECISIONS.md's own two-line summary, plus a real git commit hash (5e5fee2), that a model's synthesis can be checked against without guessing.

It has a plausible wrong answer that a shallow (single-conversation) read would produce -- e.g. concluding from local_e9841a20 alone that 0017 was 'lost' rather than 'drafted but not yet appended', which the assistant's own text there explicitly corrects.
It naturally separates retrieval (finding the mentions) from synthesis (assembling them into a chronologically and causally correct narrative) -- exactly the T1-vs-T2 distinction proposed.
